title: DPF / regen
unavailable: The DPF monitor needs a diesel profile with DPF PIDs on a CAN (UDS) link. It is hidden for petrol cars and K-line cars (no Mode 22). Select a diesel profile that has DPF values (for example the Golf Plus TDI) to use it.
allConfirmed: All DIDs confirmed on this car
experimental: ⚠ Experimental Mode 22 reads — confirm values on the car.

ok.title: DPF soot load low ({{pct}}%)
ok.detail: The particulate filter reads {{pct}}% soot: it is healthy and needs nothing.

filling.title: DPF soot building normally ({{pct}}%)
filling.detail: The particulate filter reads {{pct}}% soot. That is normal; the car burns it off on its own during a longer drive.

regenerating.title: DPF regeneration in progress
regenerating.detail: The exhaust is hot enough that the car is cleaning the particulate filter now. Keep driving at a steady speed and do not switch off until it finishes.

regen-due.title: DPF regeneration due ({{pct}}%)
regen-due.detail: The particulate filter reads {{pct}}% soot. A regeneration is due: 15–20 minutes of steady driving above 60 km/h usually starts it.

high.title: DPF soot load high ({{pct}}%)
high.detail: The particulate filter reads {{pct}}% soot. A forced or service regeneration may be needed; have it checked before the car goes into limp mode.

unknown.title: DPF soot load not read
unknown.detail: The car gave no soot-load reading, so the particulate filter could not be judged. Open DPF / regen to read it again.
